missingRules.expectedFix: Insert Contractor indemnities for third-party IP claims, legal violations, Contractor-caused data breaches, gross negligence and wilful misconduct, with standard defense procedures and IP remedies.
missingRules.note: The agreement contains no operative Contractor defense or indemnity despite the Paragraph 7 heading.

missingRules.expectedFix: Add cyber/privacy insurance and increase or clarify the limits as required by the playbook.
missingRules.note: Paragraph 14 requires workers’ compensation, CGL and professional E&O insurance, although the coverage is deficient.

missingRules.expectedFix: Add up to six months of transition assistance, machine-readable data return within 30 days and certified deletion thereafter.
missingRules.note: No post-termination transition assistance, Company Data export or certified deletion obligation is provided.

missingRules.expectedFix: Extend Company’s convenience right to outstanding Statements of Work on 30 days’ notice and remove Contractor’s 15-day convenience right.
missingRules.note: A bilateral no-cause termination right exists when no Statement of Work remains outstanding, though it is materially deficient.

missingRules.expectedFix: Add a defined warranty period and repair, re-performance, replacement or refund remedy, while preserving the express performance warranty.
missingRules.note: Contractor expressly promises professional and workmanlike performance and also gives compliance, authority and non-infringement warranties.

spans.expectedFix: Replace with New York law and exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts located in New York County.
spans.note: Arizona law is outside the playbook’s accepted governing-law jurisdictions, and no acceptable court venue is specified.

spans.expectedFix: Preferably delete the restriction; otherwise add general-solicitation and unsolicited-approach exceptions and measure 12 months from each person’s involvement.
spans.note: The mutual 12-month restriction is limited to involved personnel but lacks exceptions for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches.

spans.expectedFix: Allow Company to terminate the Agreement and any Statement of Work on 30 days’ notice with a pro-rata prepaid-fee refund, and remove Contractor’s short-notice convenience right.
spans.note: Company cannot terminate an outstanding Statement of Work for convenience, while Contractor may terminate on only 15 days’ notice between engagements.

spans.expectedFix: Permit Company assignment to affiliates and M&A successors without consent, while requiring Company consent for Contractor assignments and prohibiting assignment to a Company competitor.
spans.note: The mutual consent requirement lacks affiliate and M&A-successor assignment exceptions for Company and permits Contractor assignment with consent without a competitor restriction.

spans.expectedFix: No change is needed because the assignment places ownership of the work product with Company.
spans.note: Contractor assigns all rights in unfinished Works to Company upon termination.

spans.expectedFix: No change is needed because Vendor retention of pre-existing IP is permitted when Customer receives rights to use embedded IP.
spans.note: Contractor appropriately retains its pre-existing proprietary materials, while Company owns commissioned Works and receives a license to embedded materials elsewhere.

spans.expectedFix: No change is needed because the provision transfers the relevant work-product ownership to Company.
spans.note: Following final payment, Contractor assigns all rights in Works in progress to Company.

spans.expectedFix: No change is needed because ownership of commissioned and paid-for deliverables is allocated to Company.
spans.note: Works specifically created and paid for by Company are expressly designated as Company property.

spans.expectedFix: Make the license irrevocable and expressly usable by affiliates and contractors and transferable to an M&A successor.
spans.note: The embedded-IP license is perpetual, royalty-free and sublicensable but is not expressly irrevocable or transferable to Company’s successors.

spans.expectedFix: State that the license is perpetual, irrevocable, sublicensable to affiliates and contractors, and transferable to an M&A successor.
spans.note: Although perpetual, the license is not expressly irrevocable or transferable to a Company successor.

spans.expectedFix: Use a mutual cap equal to the greater of 12 months’ fees paid or payable and $1,000,000, with the required uncapped carve-outs.
spans.note: Contractor’s cap is limited to fees paid for the particular Services and lacks the required confidentiality, security, indemnity, misconduct, fraud and IP carve-outs.

spans.expectedFix: Replace it with the greater of 12 months’ fees paid or payable and $1,000,000 and add uncapped carve-outs for confidentiality, data protection, indemnity, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement.
spans.note: The Vendor cap may be substantially below the required 12-month-fee baseline and contains only an irrelevant Paragraph 9 carve-out.

spans.expectedFix: Add the required exceptions to the damages exclusion for confidentiality, data protection, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement.
spans.note: The mutual consequential-damages exclusion has no exceptions for confidentiality, security, indemnification, misconduct, fraud or IP infringement.

spans.expectedFix: Adopt the playbook’s mutual cap and carve-outs and clarify that Company’s undisputed payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap.
spans.note: Company’s cap is not integrated into the required mutual 12-month-fee structure and does not clarify that payment obligations are not damages.

spans.expectedFix: Add at least $2 million cyber/privacy coverage, a $2 million CGL aggregate and preferably $2 million E&O coverage, with certificates on request.
spans.note: Insurance is required, but the clause omits cyber/privacy coverage and does not specify the preferred CGL aggregate or E&O limit.
